texts: Two Factory Problems
COLOR CONFUSION — boxes repeat or miss colors, especially Sky Blue and Violet • SLOWPOKE ROBOT — the arm moves too slowly or misses crayons, causing falls, piles, jams, and stopped production.
slides.lookFor: Students can describe each symptom without adding a cause.
slides.pivot: Ask students to label each statement symptom, not solution.

images.alt: Find Your Future description of the two Robots for Crayons production problems

texts: Three Systems to Understand

COLOR SENSORS
identify colors
ROBOTIC ARMS
move and place crayons
PRODUCTION LINE
coordinates speed and flow
After each chunk, name one source-supported cause—not a final answer.
slides.lookFor: Students connect each symptom to a relevant system and keep possibilities open.
slides.pivot: Read one system at a time and ask what evidence would point toward it.

images.alt: Find Your Future reference explaining color sensors, robotic arms, and production lines

SHIFT SUPERVISOR
QUALITY CONTROL SPECIALIST
MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN
PACKAGING SUPERVISOR
Mark two clues for each problem. Record what your role would check first.
slides.lookFor: Every student marks case evidence and can explain the first check through the assigned role lens.
slides.pivot: Read the shift notes aloud and allow a private individual route.

texts: Color Confusion: Strongest Evidence

The problem began after the color sensor was replaced. Cleaning, lighting adjustment, and recalibration did not solve it.
Defensible first plan: check compatibility and installation, then run a controlled sensor test.
The software update is possible—not proven.
slides.lookFor: Students cite the replacement-sensor timing and distinguish possible from confirmed.
slides.pivot: If students call the update proof, ask what controlled test would separate the two causes.

images.alt: Find Your Future evidence used to analyze the Color Confusion case

texts: Slowpoke Robot: Strongest Evidence

The problem began after the rubber belt was changed. The reference names mismatched speed and belt tension as causes.
Defensible first plan: check belt size and tension, then retest the arm and conveyor together.
slides.lookFor: Students connect the new belt to a safe size/tension check and observable retest.
slides.pivot: Ask what a successful retest would look and sound like.

images.alt: Find Your Future machine reference used to analyze belt tension and coordinated line speed

texts: Evidence, Possible Cause, or Guess?

EVIDENCE
A source says the failure began after the belt change.
POSSIBLE CAUSE
The new belt may have the wrong size or tension.
GUESS
Replace the motor because motors break.
A plan needs evidence + a safe test.
slides.lookFor: Students sort claims correctly and can repair a guess by adding source evidence and a test.
slides.pivot: Run a three-finger check: 1 evidence, 2 possible cause, 3 guess.

images.alt: Find Your Future problem statements used to distinguish evidence from guesses

texts: Brainstorm, Then Select

Generate several safe ideas for BOTH problems.

Stop below the workbook’s 15-idea suggestion if needed to protect the final plan.

Choose the idea with:
• two case clues
• a controlled test
• an observable result
• a next check if it fails
slides.lookFor: Both problems have more than one idea before teams select a response.
slides.pivot: If brainstorming becomes random, require every new idea to connect to a marked clue.

images.alt: CCE Robots for Crayons two-problem evidence and action-plan response surface

texts: Complete Both Action Plans

EACH PROBLEM NEEDS
1. Two source clues
2. Selected solution
3. How it works
4. Three ordered steps
5. Tools or adjustments
6. Time + production effect
7. Prevention or next evidence-based check

10-minute check: evidence + one solution.
16-minute check: second ordered plan.
slides.lookFor: By minute 40, both evidence sections and one selected solution are complete; by minute 44, ordered steps exist for both.
slides.pivot: If a team cannot name a tool, test, time, or result, label the response an idea and send it back for one concrete detail.
slides.trim: Trim the brainstorm count and peer presentation before trimming either final plan.

images.alt: CCE action-plan packet with separate space for evidence, steps, tools, time, production effect, and next check

texts: Exit: Who Acts First?

Choose one Manufacturing role.
In 2-3 sentences:
Explain what that worker does first.
Cite one clue from the case.
Submit the two-problem packet. The peer presentation is optional, not required evidence this week.
slides.lookFor: The role’s first action matches the cited clue and both packet plans are collected.
slides.pivot: Accept a private oral conference or speech-to-text; record the evidence without requiring public presentation.
